headline: Highest risk is data leakage: dexter’s broad egress and secret handling can expose financial data when paired with Superset’s analytics workspace; prompt injection and conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter has autonomous execution and a scratchpad/files surface, while Superset exposes only its API and no shared channel is documented. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not provable from the profiles alone; the only plausible path would be unusual manual copy-paste or an external shared workspace, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Superset output into dexter’s scratchpad or prompt context, injected instructions can propagate.
IF both agents are connected through an external shared file or message channel, content can be reinterpreted as instructions.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted Superset output into dexter prompts.
Add a human review step before dexter executes any text sourced from Superset.
Use provenance labels on any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and requests multiple API keys, with broad network egress; Superset is an analytics tool that can surface shared data if pointed at the same workspace. The pair can therefore leak sensitive financial material through outbound API calls or dashboard outputs in default-like usage, though the profiles do not prove uncontrolled third-party exfiltration.
conditions: IF dexter is given financial or market datasets and allowed to call external APIs, those contents can leave the local boundary.
IF Superset is connected to the same sensitive dataset, its rendered outputs can expose that data to viewers or logs.
mitigations: Restrict dexter to non-sensitive sample data.
Remove unnecessary API keys from dexter’s runtime.
Limit Superset datasets to de-identified views.
Turn off verbose request/response logging.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and writes to a scratchpad, while Superset has only allowlisted egress and no write-capability overlap is documented. There is no evidence of shared filesystem, git, or database writes, so direct capability conflict is limited to unusual shared-resource setups.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or mutable dataset, their outputs can collide.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same stateful resource without locking, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid shared mutable databases or git repos.
Run only one writer per resource at a time.
Use file locks or job locks where shared state is unavoidable.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is autonomous and can generate research outputs from external APIs; Superset can present those outputs in analytics workflows. If Superset treats dexter’s results as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into dashboards or decisions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Superset ingests dexter-produced facts without validation, incorrect research can be rendered as trusted analytics.
IF downstream users act on Superset dashboards derived from dexter outputs, a single upstream error can propagate.
mitigations: Require source links for every dexter-derived claim.
Add a manual verification step before dashboard publication.
Mark dexter outputs as untrusted until reviewed.
Compare key figures against an independent source.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tracking from dexter into Superset.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and handles multiple API keys, while Superset is an analytics platform with no residency or retention controls shown. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around logging, retention, or regulated financial data handling, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdictional breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed through Superset or dexter logs, retention or access controls may diverge.
IF either system stores outputs longer than the source-data policy allows, compliance obligations can be violated.
mitigations: Classify financial data before routing it.
Shorten log retention on both systems.
Restrict access to approved operators only.
Document the data flow between dexter and Superset.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
